source.title: Building Auditable AI Text Detectors with Sparse Autoencoders
source.authors: Liam Dugan; Callum McDougall; M. Denton; Philip Pham; Christine Kaeser-Chen; Christopher Callison-Burch

record.tranche_reason: The study uses sparse-autoencoder features and auto-interpreted descriptions to build AI-text detectors, but does not test claims about individual neurons or neuron explanations.
record.gate_note: The study's measured units are SAE features extracted from Gemma-2-2B residual-stream activations, not the model's individual neurons. Its neuron-polysemanticity statements are background; it reports no Qwen3-32B neuron-pole audit, cross-model neuron shares, InceptionV1 examples, or neuron-based attribution graphs. The SAE-description results below are related but do not measure the claim versions' neuron-level outcomes.
record.test_reason: The study builds AI-text detectors from sparse-autoencoder features of Gemma-2-2B's residual stream, with auto-interp descriptions filtered by a simulation-score threshold. It reports detector performance and paraphrase ablations. It never audits individual neurons. It reports no neuron-pole shares, no cross-model neuron shares, no InceptionV1 examples and no neuron-based attribution graphs. Its auto-interp scores are for SAE features, not neurons. Its statement that neurons are polysemantic is background citing Olah et al. 2020, not a result.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that SAE features filtered by auto-interp score yield auditable detectors. These match the underlying neural detector (FT-Model+SAE), and base-model SAE classifiers generalize better out of distribution. They also report that the conclusion claims the descriptions have both high recall and high precision, while the Limitations section concedes a recall bias and notes they tested only GemmaScope SAEs on Gemma-2-2B.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains or fine-tunes SAEs on a detector's residual stream, generates descriptions for SAE features, filters features by simulation score, and trains a logistic-regression detector; it does not audit individual neurons or construct attribution graphs.

fits_no_version.finding: In an informal regex check of a subset of SAE-feature descriptions, about half reached 99.5+ F1. The rest showed recall bias to varying degrees.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Auto-interp descriptions of SAE features that pass simulation-score validation are often high-recall but low-precision, analogous to V6 but for SAE features.

fits_no_version.finding: Agreement between zero-ablation and paraphrase-removal logit effects rises with auto-interp score, from rho 0.78 in the lowest quartile to 0.87 in the highest (Table 10).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Higher simulation scores for SAE-feature descriptions predict more faithful causal editing of those features.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 2026 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
record.problems: The regex assessment is described as informal, and the authors state they tested only fine-tuned GemmaScope SAEs rather than SAEs on other base models. These limitations concern SAE features and do not provide direct evidence about the claim's neuron-level versions.
record.rows_left_out: No claim-version rows were available: detector performance, paraphrase ablations, and SAE-feature simulation results do not measure neuron-level interpretability or neuron-explanation accuracy.

record.verdict_notes: The record's T4 classification and the not_tested status for all versions are correct. Nothing here bears on neuron-level claims, because SAE features are explicitly used in place of neurons. The study is not one of the originals, though it cites Bills et al. 2023 for its method.

rows.subject: SAE features (subset; base model and condition not stated)
rows.operation_detail: Informal evaluation of generated feature descriptions using regular expressions intended to match the descriptions
rows.measure: F1 of regex matches against an unspecified ground truth; description precision and recall
rows.value: Roughly half of the features had perfect descriptions (99.5+ F1 score); the other half showed recall bias to varying degrees.
rows.locator: Limitations, “Feature descriptions are biased towards recall”
rows.note: The authors describe this as an informal assessment of a subset of SAE features. It evaluates SAE-feature descriptions, not neuron explanations or neuron firing.
rows.check: This row measures SAE-feature descriptions, not neuron explanations, so it bears on no version. The subject should read: SAE features from Gemma-2-2B (GemmaScope, possibly fine-tuned), unspecified subset. The baseline is LLM-generated regexes used as ground truth. The assessment is informal, so 'partial' against a claim version is not meaningful.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
